source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 decembrie — «Sfântul Mucenic Mina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Μηνάς ο Καλλικέλαδος, Ερμογένης και Εύγραφος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the Athenian of pagan family who was made eparch of Alexandria, refused to carry out the persecution, and was beheaded with the two who were converted by his answer. The entry names all three of its members, each with his own couplet, and the corpus already keeps all three, so this day is three upgrades and no new folder. **The page will not settle the reign**: «ο βασιλιάς Μαξιμίνος (311 - 313 μ.Χ.) (κατ' άλλους ο Μαξιμιανός [286 - 305 μ.Χ])», Maximinus or, according to others, Maximian — two reigns a generation apart, so no `dates` object is proposed and the folder's dateless state stands. The page prints two apolytikia, a kontakion and a kathisma. The first apolytikion, «Δι' ἐγκρατείας», speaks of the martyrs of Christ in the plural and is the common of their service, so it is copied into each of the three folders; the second, «Ἡ καλλικέλαδος», and the kontakion both address Menas by name and are taken here only. The kathisma is not a kind the schema holds. The page's relics block — the incorrupt tongue at the monastery of Leimonos on Lesbos, and portions at Docheiariou and at the Benaki Museum — stands under the heading of Eugraphus and does not say whose it is, so it is recorded here and not drafted. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.12.2025 (10. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Мина, Ермоген и Евграф.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, AN ENUMERATED THREE, so BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 counts three and each of the three folders takes this one heading whole with its closing full stop; the corpus holds all three. URL year 2025. He is the first name. `types` UNTOUCHED: «мученици» is the `martyr` held. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND STILL ABSENT, AND THE REFUSAL IS DELIBERATE: the entry names the emperor «Максимин» and gives his reign no years, so there was no interval to take and BRIEF.md §4 forbids making one; the folder had no `dates` and still has none. NO `locations`: Athens, Constantinople and Alexandria are three places and the folder has never held a coordinate. NO `related` ROW ADDED: `hermogenes-of-alexandria` and `eugraphus` are already `related` here in both directions and are the only persons the entry names besides the emperor. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, where the Romanian and Greek lines gave three names: that he and Hermogenes were Athenians by birth and both in great honour at Constantinople; that he was known for his learning and his eloquence and OUTWARDLY PASSED FOR A PAGAN WHILE BEING A CONVINCED CHRISTIAN IN HIS HEART; that the emperor sent him to Alexandria to quiet a riot and root Christianity out, and that he made the peace and then declared himself a Christian and converted many; that Hermogenes, sent to punish him, cut off his feet and his tongue and put out his eyes and threw him in prison, where the Lord Jesus himself appeared and healed him; and that the sight of that healing is what made Hermogenes a Christian. Their relics were thrown into the sea and came by a wonder to Constantinople, where the bishop, warned in a dream, met them and buried them honourably. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Cu înfrânarea omorând pornirile și îndemnurile cele arzătoare ale patimilor, ucenicii lui Hristos au luat harul de a alunga urmările bolilor celor neputincioși și a face minuni, atât în viață, cât și după moarte. Minune uimitoare cu adevărat! Că oase goale izvorăsc tămăduiri. Slavă Ție, Singurului Dumnezeu și Ziditorului.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Mina, Ermoghen și Evgraf (one hymn printed for the three together; the page prints no glas)

english.text: Having put to death by abstinence the burning stirrings and promptings of the passions, the disciples of Christ received the grace to drive away the effects of the sicknesses of the infirm and to work wonders, both in life and after death. A marvel indeed: that bare bones pour out healings. Glory to you, the only God and Maker.

hymns.text: Δι' ἐγκρατείας, τῶν παθῶν τὰς πυριφλέκτους, ἀπονεκρώσαντες ὁρμὰς καὶ τὰς κινήσεις, τοῦ Χριστοῦ οἱ Μάρτυρες ἔλαβον τὴν χάριν, τὰς νόσους ἀποδιώκειν τῶν ἀσθενῶν, καὶ ζῶντες καὶ μετὰ τέλος θαυματουργεῖν· ὄντως θαῦμα παράδοξον! ὅτι ὀστέα γυμνά, ἐκβλύζουσιν ἰάματα. Δόξα τῷ μόνῳ Θεῷ ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τὸ προσταχθὲν — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Μηνάς ο Καλλικέλαδος, Ερμογένης και Εύγραφος»; it is the common of the three martyrs, in the plural, printed as their service.

english.text: Having put to death by abstinence the fire-burning rushes and motions of the passions, the martyrs of Christ received the grace to drive away the diseases of the sick and to work wonders both while they lived and after their end. Truly a strange wonder, that bare bones should pour out healings! Glory to our only God.

hymns.text: Ἡ καλλικέλαδος, θεόφρον γλῶσσα σου, λαμπρῶς κηρύξασα, Χριστοῦ τὴν σάρκωσιν, συναθλητᾶς σοὶ εὐκλεεῖς, εἰλκύσατο ἐν σταδίῳ, Μηνᾷ παμμακάριστε, Ἐρμογένην τὸν ἔνδοξον, καὶ τὸν θεῖον Εὔγραφον, μεθ' ὧν χαίρων ἠγώνισαι. Καὶ νῦν τὴν Παναγίαν Τριάδα, ὑπὲρ ἠμῶν ἐκδυσωπεῖτε.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Τὴν ὡραιότητα — the second hymn on the page of the three martyrs of 10 Δεκεμβρίου; it addresses Menas by name and names the other two as his fellow contestants.

english.text: Your sweet-sounding, God-minded tongue, splendidly proclaiming the incarnation of Christ, drew to you in the stadium illustrious fellow contestants, all-blessed Menas — the glorious Hermogenes and the divine Eugraphus, with whom you rejoicing contended. And now entreat the all-holy Trinity on our behalf.

hymns.text: Τῆς στρατείας ἥρπασε, σὲ τῆς προσκαίρου, καὶ ἀφθάρτου ἔδειξε, συγκληρονόμον ὦ Μηνᾶ, σὺν τοῖς συνάθλοις σου Κύριος, ὁ παρασχών σοι τὸν ἄφθαρτον στέφανον.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον — on the page of the three martyrs of 10 Δεκεμβρίου, and it addresses Menas by name.

english.text: The Lord snatched you from the temporary service and showed you a fellow heir of the incorruptible one, Menas, together with your fellow contestants — he who gave you the incorruptible crown.
